title: Species richness of Eurasian Zephyrus hairstreaks with implications on historical biogeography
author: Hailing Zhuang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jr2cm8e
materials: Installed the software DIVA-GIS 7.5, NDM/VNDM 3 and Adobe Photoshop CS6 for Win7 system. Free vector and raster map data with WGS84 projection at 1:10m scale from public domain http://www.naturalearthdata.com/downloads/ for generating background world map and Whole world - land and oceans image that from Visible Earth https://visibleearth.nasa.gov/view.php?id=57752

steps.title: Construct species distribution database
steps.instruction: Compile species records from literature published prior to 2016 into a Microsoft Excel 97-2003 sheet, ensuring validity of geographical distribution and taxonomic information.

substeps.instruction: Organize data columns as: ID, Species, Latitude, Longitude, Country, ADM, and References.

steps.title: Process data in DIVA-GIS 7.5
steps.instruction: Upload the species dataset to DIVA-GIS 7.5 and prepare the spatial layers.

substeps.instruction: Transform the .xls file to .shp format.
Add the background map data layer.
Test the species accumulation curve at the genus level to ensure adequate sampling.

steps.title: Calculate species richness
steps.instruction: Generate richness maps using the point-to-grid analysis tool in DIVA-GIS 7.5.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to Analysis -> point to grid -> richness.
Set Parameters -> Field to 'SPECIES'.
Define a new grid with a 3° × 3° cell size in the Main section.
Select 'Richness' as the Output Variable.
Select 'Number of different classes (Richness)' to count different classes per cell size.
Provide a list of conditioned equal interval values and scale.
Add the latitude-longitude grid for visualization.
Export the resulting images.

steps.title: Recode database for VNDM/NDM
steps.instruction: Use VNDM/NDM Version 3 (Goloboff, 2005) to recode the database into .xyd suffix format.

steps.title: Analyze Areas of Endemism (AOEs)
steps.instruction: Perform AOE analysis using grid cells of 2° and 3° for each species and genus level, starting from original position x=66.860, Y=59.883.

substeps.instruction: Set parameters based on Prado et al. (2015) with modifications.
Configure search settings: repeat search 100 times, temporary sets within 0.99 of current score, and save sets with two or more endemic species.
Set score thresholds: above 2.0 for genus-level analysis and above 3.0 for species-level analysis.
Swap cells one at a time.
Define overlapping subsets as those where 50% of species are unique.
Select an upper minimum score of 0.3 (Escalante et al., 2013).
Compute consensus AOEs using a cut-off of 50% similarity at different taxonomic levels using flexible consensus (Szumik et al., 2002).

steps.title: Visualize and reconstruct distribution maps
steps.instruction: Export and visualize the distribution of generated AOEs and genus patterns.

substeps.instruction: Export the file format from DIVA-GIS from NDA of each generated AOE to visualize the distribution map.
Generate distribution maps for each genus using DIVA-GIS.
Classify different distributions and integrate similar distribution pattern species databases to reconstruct the distribution pattern.
